person: CJ Moulton is a senior software engineer in Clementon, New Jersey. He designs and maintains automated test frameworks for mission-critical software, and he works with other teams so integration, regression, and end-to-end testing stay reliable.
He earned an M.S. in Computer Science and a B.S. in Computer Science with a minor in Cyber Security from Felician University.
company: Moulton Ventures is his holding company. Moulton is the public name on the work.

bio: I am passionate about continuously learning and adapting to achieve both personal and organizational goals.

I design and maintain automated test frameworks for mission-critical software, and I collaborate across teams to make integration, regression, and end-to-end testing reliable. I earned an M.S. in Computer Science and a B.S. in Computer Science with a minor in Cyber Security from Felician University.

experience.summary: Software development, software testing, and software integration for mission-critical systems.
highlights: Designed and maintained automated test frameworks using Python, JSON, and Bash to validate mission-critical software across multiple environments.
Led cross-organization collaboration between ASRC Federal and Lockheed Martin to integrate automation frameworks using Sikuli and Robot Framework, improving test coverage and reuse.
Built automation supporting system integration, end-to-end, and regression testing under live and simulated conditions.
Improved performance, portability, and maintainability of automation tools across diverse system configurations.
Collaborated with software and systems engineers to define test requirements, troubleshoot integration issues, and improve system reliability.
Developed automated testing pipelines to streamline validation workflows and reduce manual effort.
Delivered technical reports and analysis supporting high-stakes test events and program milestones.

experience.summary: Selected for the First Flyer program, an accelerated path for recent graduates. Rotational assignments covered the IT department and the mortgage industry, and this role was my introduction to Agile Scrum.
highlights: Queried and analyzed loan and customer data using Oracle SQL to support application validation and reporting.
Wrote Jira user stories, acceptance criteria, and test cases with developers and product teams.
Performed regression and user-acceptance testing for loan disclosure and underwriting systems before production releases.
Tested and validated InRule business rules so data stayed accurate across internal systems.
Created, developed, and maintained reports using Jira and Tableau.
Coordinated daily and weekly cross-team syncs during rotational assignments.
Supported identity and access management, including secure enterprise authentication distribution.
Assisted with system and network monitoring using QRadar, Palo Alto, and Symantec.
Prepared and presented weekly technical summaries to management and stakeholders.

experience.summary: Second internship, with the Information Security team. Focused on network management and application security.
highlights: Monitored company traffic with QRadar and Palo Alto.
Scanned for phishing emails and malicious links.
Configured firewall rules and conditions.
Compiled and presented weekly reports on significant changes in security data.

experience.location: Started from a college dorm room
experience.summary: Founded RYLTY (pronounced Royalty) just before sophomore year. The brand began with apparel, then moved into jewelry and accessories after dropping the apparel line.
highlights: Partnered with international manufacturers to offer custom jewelry in gold, white gold, 925 sterling silver, platinum, and GIA-certified diamonds (SI–VVS clarity).
Used the internet and social media to reach customers, which started a lasting interest in entrepreneurship.

experience.summary: First internship. Managed and analyzed mortgage loan data and presented findings to management.
highlights: Analyzed mortgage loan data and presented findings with Tableau and PowerPoint.
Worked with colleagues to identify and depict data trends used in decision-making.
Built a foundation in industry tools that later roles kept expanding.
